text_blocks.snippet: Common active scams reported across Central Illinois include fake text messages about unpaid traffic or toll violations, pre-trial release phone scams, and fraudulent package delivery alerts. Scammers frequently use artificial intelligence and spoofed local numbers to create a false sense of urgency.
Active Scam Types in Central Illinois

list.snippet:
Fake Traffic and Toll Texts: Fraudulent messages claiming unpaid fines from transit or toll agencies threaten license suspension if you do not click a payment link (warned by the Office of the Illinois Attorney General
).
Pre-Trial Release Extortion: Scammers call or email victims claiming a relative is in jail and demanding immediate cash via apps like Zelle or Cash App to pay for GPS monitoring or bail.
Delivery and Porch Pirate Alerts: Texts claiming a package cannot be delivered due to a missing address number, prompting users to click a malicious link to verify personal details.
Pen Pal and Impersonation Cons: Unsolicited texts mimic friendly contacts or family members in distress, eventually asking for gift cards or wire transfers.
Practice the Pause: Stop and take time to verify any urgent request before sending money or sharing details.
Never Click Links: Do not open links or call numbers provided in unsolicited texts about fines or packages.
Verify Independently: Government and transit agencies do not text or call unprompted demanding immediate payment. Look up official contact numbers independently to check status.
Report Fraud: If targeted, report incidents to the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois or forward scam texts to state authorities.
